definition.text: A West Germanic language that developed from 17th-century Dutch in southern Africa; an official language of South Africa, also spoken in Namibia.
The language of the indigenous Ainu people of Hokkaido and nearby islands; unrelated to Japanese and critically endangered, with revival efforts under way.
A Kwa language of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire made up of closely related varieties such as Twi and Fante; one of Ghana's most widely spoken languages.
The Indo-European language of Albania and Kosovo, forming its own branch of the family, with Gheg and Tosk dialect groups; the standard is based on Tosk.

The natural sign language of the Deaf community in the United States and much of English-speaking Canada, with a grammar of its own distinct from English; used in interpreting, Deaf education and accessibility work.
A Semitic language and the working federal language of Ethiopia, written in an Ethiopic (Ge'ez-derived) script.
A Semitic language of the Arab world and the liturgical language of Islam; Modern Standard Arabic serves writing and formal media while spoken regional varieties differ widely.
The Indo-European language of Armenia, forming its own branch of the family and written in the Armenian alphabet; standard Eastern and Western forms exist.
An Indo-Aryan language of Assam in northeastern India and the state's official language, written in a variant of the Bengali-Assamese script.
An Aymaran language of the Andean altiplano in Bolivia, Peru and Chile; official in Bolivia and Peru.
A Turkic language of Azerbaijan and northwestern Iran, written in Latin script in Azerbaijan and in Perso-Arabic script in Iran.
A Kru language of Liberia spoken by the Bassa people, which has its own indigenous Vah script.

flags.note: The label does not say whether it means the Liberian Kru language Bassa or the Bantu language Basaa of Cameroon; the Liberian language is assumed.

definition.text: A group of related Austronesian languages of northern Sumatra, Indonesia, including Toba, Karo, Simalungun and Mandailing, historically written in a Batak script.

flags.note: The label names a cluster of languages rather than one language.

definition.text: A Bantu language of northern Zambia and neighboring areas, widely used as a regional lingua franca in Zambia.
A small Bantu language of coastal Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.
An Indo-Aryan language of Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal, the national language of Bangladesh, written in the Bengali script.
The family of Afroasiatic languages indigenous to North Africa, including Tashelhit, Kabyle, Tamazight and Tuareg varieties.

flags.note: The label names a language family; work listings usually mean a specific variety such as Tashelhit or Kabyle.

definition.text: An English-based creole and national language of Vanuatu, used as a lingua franca among the country's many local languages.
A South Slavic language standard used chiefly by Bosniaks in Bosnia and Herzegovina, mutually intelligible with Croatian and Serbian.
The Sino-Tibetan language and official language of Myanmar, written in the Burmese script.
A Cariban language, also called Kari'nja, spoken by the Carib people along the northern coast of South America in Suriname, Guyana, French Guiana, Venezuela and Brazil.

flags.note: The label may also be read as the wider Carib language family or as the Antillean language historically called Island Carib.

definition.text: The Spanish of Castile, taken as the standard form in Spain and often used as another name for Spanish in contrast to other Spanish-language varieties and regional languages of Spain.

flags.note: Likely an alias or regional label for Spanish rather than a separate language; kept separate by ID as in the roster.

definition.text: A Romance language of Catalonia, Valencia, the Balearic Islands, Andorra and nearby areas; official in Andorra and co-official in several regions of Spain.
An Austronesian language of the central Philippines, widely spoken in Cebu, Bohol, eastern Negros and parts of Mindanao.
An Indo-Aryan language of the Chakma people in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh and in northeastern India, traditionally written in its own script.
An Austronesian language of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, official there alongside English and rich in Spanish loan vocabulary.
A Bantu language of Malawi and neighboring parts of Zambia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe; the national language of Malawi.
The family of Sinitic languages of the Han Chinese, including Mandarin, Cantonese, Wu and Min, which share a writing system of Chinese characters.

flags.note: The label names a family; in work listings it usually means Mandarin, written in simplified or traditional characters.

definition.text: A West Slavic language of the Czech Republic, written in the Latin alphabet with diacritics.
A North Germanic language of Denmark, also spoken in Greenland and the Faroe Islands and partly intelligible with Norwegian and Swedish.
The variety of Persian that is an official language of Afghanistan, also called Afghan Persian.
An Indo-Aryan language and national language of the Maldives, written right to left in the Thaana script.
A Nilotic language cluster of South Sudan spoken by the Dinka people, with several dialects that differ considerably.
A Bantu language of the Duala people of coastal Cameroon, historically a trade language around the Wouri estuary.
A West Germanic language of the Netherlands and Flanders in Belgium, and an official language of Suriname.
The Tibetic national language of Bhutan, written in the Tibetan script.
A West Germanic language that serves as a leading international language of business, science, aviation and the internet, with national standards such as American and British English.
A Bantu language of the Beti group spoken in the Yaoundé region of southern Cameroon.
A name used for the language or languages of the Fali people of northern Cameroon and northeastern Nigeria.

flags.note: Several distinct Adamawa languages are called Fali and the label does not say which; the definition is deliberately minimal.

definition.text: The national language of the Philippines, a standardized register based on Tagalog and enriched with words from other Philippine languages, Spanish and English.
A Uralic language of Finland, agglutinative with many noun cases and unrelated to the Indo-European languages around it; official in Finland alongside Swedish.
A Romance language spoken on several continents and an official language in many countries and international bodies such as the United Nations and the European Union.
A group of West Germanic languages of the Netherlands, Germany and Denmark, of which West Frisian in the Dutch province of Friesland is the most widely spoken.
A Niger-Congo language of the Fulani people spoken in a belt across West and Central Africa from Senegal to Cameroon.
A Goidelic Celtic language of Scotland (Scottish Gaelic), or more loosely the Goidelic branch that also includes Irish and Manx.

flags.note: The label can mean Scottish Gaelic, Irish or Manx; the intended language is not specified.

definition.text: A Tani language of the Sino-Tibetan family spoken by the Galo people of Arunachal Pradesh in northeastern India.
An Arawakan language of the Garifuna people on the Caribbean coast of Honduras, Belize, Guatemala and Nicaragua.
A West Germanic language of Germany, Austria and much of Switzerland, widely used in business, engineering and science; standard German coexists with regional dialects.
A Bantu language of the Kikuyu people of central Kenya, the first language of Kenya's largest ethnic group.
The Indo-European language of Greece and Cyprus, written in the Greek alphabet; Modern Greek descends from Ancient Greek.

flags.note: Presumed to mean Modern Greek unless a listing says Ancient or Koine Greek.

definition.text: An Indo-Aryan language of the Indian state of Gujarat, written in the Gujarati script and widely spoken in diaspora communities.
A French-based creole that is the national language of Haiti and the first language of most Haitians.
A Chadic language spoken as a first language and widely as a trade language across northern Nigeria, Niger and the Sahel.
A dialect of Kannada spoken by the Havyaka Brahmin community of coastal and Malnad Karnataka, with distinctive vocabulary and sounds.

flags.note: A dialect of Kannada rather than a separate language.

definition.text: A Polynesian language of Hawaii, official in the state alongside English and revitalized through immersion schooling since the 1980s.
A Bantu language of the Haya people of the Kagera region of northwestern Tanzania.
A Semitic language; Modern Hebrew is the national language of Israel, revived from the literary and liturgical Hebrew of earlier periods.
An Indo-Aryan language of northern and central India written in the Devanagari script, one of India's official languages and among the most widely spoken in the world.
A group of Hmong-Mien languages of the Hmong people of southern China, Laos, Vietnam and Thailand and of diaspora communities, notably White Hmong and Green Hmong.

flags.note: The label names a cluster of related languages rather than a single one.

definition.text: A Southern Min variety of Chinese from southern Fujian, spoken across Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asian communities.
A Uto-Aztecan language of the Hopi people of northeastern Arizona.
A Uralic language of Hungary and Hungarian communities in neighboring countries; agglutinative and unrelated to its Indo-European neighbors.
A Naduhup language of the Vaupés region of Brazil and Colombia, spoken by the Hupda people.
A Niger-Congo tonal language of southeastern Nigeria and one of the country's major languages.
The national language of Indonesia, a standardized form of Malay used as a lingua franca across the archipelago and written in the Latin alphabet.
A Romance language of Italy and parts of Switzerland, descended from Tuscan and widely studied for its use in arts, music, cuisine and trade.
The language of Japan, written with a mix of kanji and the kana scripts and marked by a system of honorific speech levels.
A small Jukunoid language of eastern Nigeria, also called Jibu.

flags.note: Identification is from memory and should be checked against a language catalogue; the definition is deliberately minimal.

definition.text: The Jingpho language, a Sino-Tibetan language of the Kachin people of northern Myanmar and neighboring parts of India and China.
A group of closely related Nilotic languages of western Kenya, including Kipsigis, Nandi and Tugen.

flags.note: The label names a cluster of related languages.

definition.text: A Dravidian language of Karnataka in southern India, its official language, written in the Kannada script.
A Turkic language, official in Kazakhstan and also spoken in China and Mongolia, written in Cyrillic in Kazakhstan.
The Austroasiatic official language of Cambodia, written in the Khmer script.
A Bantu language of Rwanda, spoken by nearly all Rwandans and an official language there, closely related to Kirundi.
A Bantu language and official language of Burundi, mutually intelligible with Kinyarwanda.
A Tibeto-Burman language of Tripura in northeastern India and parts of Bangladesh, official in Tripura alongside Bengali and English.
The language of Korea, written in the Hangul alphabet and marked by speech levels that encode social relationship.
An Austroasiatic language of the Munda branch spoken by the Korwa people of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh in India.
A group of Northwestern Iranian languages of the Kurds in Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria, of which Kurmanji and Sorani are the main varieties.

flags.note: The label names a dialect continuum; Kurmanji and Sorani differ in script and grammar.

definition.text: A Dravidian language of the Oraon people of eastern India, in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal, and of Nepal and Bangladesh.
A Turkic language, official in Kyrgyzstan, written in Cyrillic.
A Judeo-Spanish language of Sephardic Jews, descended from medieval Spanish with Hebrew and other loan words; now endangered.
A Western Nilotic language of the Lango people of northern Uganda, related to Luo languages.
A Tai-Kadai language and the official language of Laos, closely related to Thai and written in the Lao script.
An Austroasiatic language of the Lawa people of northern Thailand, in Mae Hong Son and Chiang Mai provinces.

flags.note: The label is minimal; the Thai Lawa (Lua') language is assumed and the identification is from memory.

definition.text: A Bantu language of the Congo River basin, a lingua franca across the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo and widely used in music and the military.
A West Germanic language that is the national language of Luxembourg, used alongside French and German in administration and daily life.
A South Slavic language, the official language of North Macedonia, written in the Cyrillic alphabet.
An Indo-Aryan language of the Mithila region of Bihar in India and southeastern Nepal, one of India's scheduled languages.
An Austronesian language and an official language of Madagascar, most closely related to languages of southern Borneo.
A Dravidian language of Kerala in southern India, the state's official language, written in its own script.
A Semitic language of Malta written in the Latin alphabet, with large Italian and English vocabularies; official in Malta and the European Union.
The Sinitic language group and standard spoken Chinese based on Beijing pronunciation; Standard Mandarin is the national standard in mainland China and Taiwan and an official language of Singapore.
A Tibeto-Burman language of Manipur in northeastern India, written in the Meitei Mayek and Bengali scripts.
A Goidelic Celtic language of the Isle of Man that lost its last native speakers in the 20th century and is being revived through classes and schools.
An Indo-Aryan language of Maharashtra in western India, the state's official language, written in Devanagari.
A family of about thirty languages of Mexico, Guatemala, Belize and Honduras, including K'iche', Yucatec and Q'eqchi'.

flags.note: The label names a language family rather than a single language.

definition.text: A Tibeto-Burman Kuki-Chin language of Mizoram in northeastern India, the state's principal language, written in the Latin alphabet.
A Mongolic language of Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, written in Cyrillic in Mongolia and in the traditional vertical script in China.
The name of two Bantu languages of the Nguni group: Southern Ndebele of South Africa and Northern Ndebele of Zimbabwe, which is closely related to Zulu.

flags.note: The label does not say whether the South African or the Zimbabwean language is meant.

definition.text: An Indo-Aryan language and the official language of Nepal, written in Devanagari and also spoken in Sikkim, Darjeeling and Bhutan.
A North Germanic language of Norway with two written standards, Bokmål and Nynorsk, largely intelligible with Danish and Swedish.
An Indo-Aryan language of Odisha in eastern India, a classical language of India written in the Odia script.
A group of Bantu languages of the Ovambo people of northern Namibia and southern Angola, notably Kwanyama and Ndonga.

flags.note: The label names a cluster of closely related varieties.

definition.text: An Eastern Iranian language of the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan, an official language of Afghanistan, written in an Arabic-based script.
A Western Iranian language of Iran, Afghanistan and Tajikistan, written in an Arabic-based script in Iran and Afghanistan, with national varieties Farsi, Dari and Tajik.
An extinct Northwest Semitic language of the Phoenician city-states of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos, written in the Phoenician alphabet from which later alphabets descend.
A West Slavic language of Poland, written in the Latin alphabet with diacritics.
A Romance language of Portugal, Brazil and several African countries, with European and Brazilian standards.
An Indo-Aryan language of the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, written in Gurmukhi in India and in the Shahmukhi script in Pakistan.
A family of Quechuan languages of the Andes spoken from Colombia to Argentina, with most speakers in Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador and official status in Peru and Bolivia.

flags.note: The label names a language family whose varieties are not all mutually intelligible.

definition.text: A Romance language and the official language of Romania and Moldova.

An East Slavic language written in Cyrillic, official in Russia and several neighboring countries, widely used across the former Soviet states and one of the six official languages of the United Nations.
A Turkic language of the Sakha Republic in Siberia, where it is official alongside Russian.
A Polynesian language of Samoa and American Samoa with distinct formal and colloquial registers.
A creole-like language based on Ngbandi that is the national language and lingua franca of the Central African Republic, official alongside French.
A Munda language of the Austroasiatic family spoken by the Santal people of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha, written in the Ol Chiki script and a scheduled language of India.
An Indo-Aryan language of southern Punjab and neighboring areas of Pakistan, closely related to Punjabi and Sindhi.
The South Slavic language continuum underlying the Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin and Serbian standards, which differ chiefly in vocabulary, script use and some forms.

flags.note: A pluricentric label that overlaps the national standards listed separately in the roster.

definition.text: A Bantu language of Lesotho and South Africa, official in both countries.
A Tai language of Shan State in Myanmar, related to Thai and Lao and written in a script derived from Burmese.
A group of closely related Bantu languages that are the principal languages of Zimbabwe, including Karanga, Zezuru and Manyika.

flags.note: The label names a cluster of related varieties with a standardized written form.

definition.text: A West Slavic language or dialect of Upper Silesia in Poland and Czechia, regarded by some as a Polish dialect and by others as a separate language.

flags.note: Its status as a separate language is disputed.

definition.text: An Indo-Aryan language of Sindh in Pakistan and of communities in India, written in an Arabic-based script in Pakistan and in Devanagari in India.
An Indo-Aryan language of Sri Lanka, the majority and an official language there, written in the Sinhala script.
A West Slavic language and the official language of Slovakia, closely related to Czech.
A South Slavic language of Slovenia, notable for retaining a dual grammatical number.
An extinct Eastern Iranian language of Sogdiana in Central Asia, a language of Silk Road trade and of Manichaean and Buddhist texts.
A Cushitic language of Somalia and neighboring regions of Ethiopia, Djibouti and Kenya, written in the Latin alphabet since 1972.
A Romance language that is the first language of Spain and most of Latin America, a major international language in business, media and public services.
An extinct language isolate of ancient Mesopotamia written in cuneiform, the earliest attested written language, studied by Assyriologists.
An Austronesian language of western Java in Indonesia.
An Alemannic German dialect of Swabia in Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria, Germany.

flags.note: A dialect of German rather than a separate language.

definition.text: A Bantu language and lingua franca of East Africa, official in Tanzania and Kenya and widely used as a trade and media language.
A Bantu language of the Nguni group, official in Eswatini and South Africa.
A North Germanic language of Sweden, also an official language of Finland, written in the Latin alphabet.
The variety of Persian that is the official language of Tajikistan, written in Cyrillic.
A Dravidian classical language of Tamil Nadu in India and of Sri Lanka, official in India's Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka and Singapore, with its own script.
A Turkic language of the Tatar people, spoken chiefly in Tatarstan and elsewhere in Russia.
A Dravidian language of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in India, written in the Telugu script.
A tonal Tai-Kadai language and the official language of Thailand, written in the Thai script.
The Indo-Aryan speech of the Tharu people of the Terai lowlands of Nepal and northern India.

flags.note: Several related varieties share the name; the label does not specify one.

definition.text: A Sino-Tibetan language of Tibet and neighboring regions, written in the Tibetan script, with Central, Kham and Amdo varieties.
A Semitic language of Eritrea and the Tigray region of Ethiopia, written in the Ge'ez script.
A Bantu language of Botswana and South Africa, the national language of Botswana.
A Dravidian language of coastal Karnataka and northern Kerala in India.
A Turkic language, the official language of Turkey, written in a Latin alphabet since 1928.
A Turkic language and the official language of Turkmenistan, written in the Latin alphabet.
An East Slavic language and the official language of Ukraine, written in Cyrillic.
An Indo-Aryan language, the national language of Pakistan, written in a Perso-Arabic script and mutually intelligible with Hindi in everyday speech.
A Turkic language of the Uyghur people of Xinjiang in China and of Central Asian communities, mainly written in an Arabic-based script.
A Turkic language and the official language of Uzbekistan, written mainly in the Latin alphabet.
A tonal Austroasiatic language and the official language of Vietnam, written in a Latin-based alphabet with diacritics.
An Indo-Aryan Bhil language of the Vagad region of southern Rajasthan and neighboring areas of India.

flags.note: Identification and region are from memory and should be checked against a language catalogue.

definition.text: A Romance language of the langue d'oïl group spoken in Wallonia in Belgium.
A Bantu language of the Nguni group, widely spoken in South Africa's Eastern Cape and noted for its click consonants; one of South Africa's official languages.
A Niger-Congo tonal language of southwestern Nigeria and neighboring Benin and Togo, written in the Latin alphabet with tone marks.
A Bantu language of the Nguni group and the most widely spoken home language in South Africa, one of its official languages.

SAP's proprietary programming language for writing reports, interfaces, extensions and applications on the SAP application server; developers use it to implement business logic and read and update SAP data.
An object-oriented scripting language derived from ECMAScript, used with Adobe Flash and AIR to build interactive animations, games and rich internet applications.
A statically and strongly typed language designed for reliable, long-lived embedded and safety-critical systems in aviation, defense and rail, with built-in tasking for concurrency.
The 1995 revision of Ada (ISO/IEC 8652:1995), which added object-oriented programming, protected types and hierarchical libraries to Ada 83.
A research language, known as ALF, that integrates functional and logic programming through equational definitions and logic-style search.

flags.note: A niche research language identified from memory; the definition is deliberately brief.

definition.text: A family of early imperative languages, including ALGOL 60 and ALGOL 68, that introduced block structure and formal grammar notation and shaped Pascal, C and later languages; used in algorithm publication and teaching.
Salesforce Marketing Cloud's scripting language embedded in emails, landing pages and messages to personalize content, look up data and apply conditional logic.
Salesforce's strongly typed, Java-like language that runs on the Salesforce platform; developers write triggers, classes and batch jobs to implement business logic and integrations.

A low-level language of mnemonics that map nearly one-to-one to a processor's machine instructions, used for firmware, drivers, performance-critical routines, reverse engineering and learning computer architecture.
A small text-processing language that applies pattern-action rules to lines and fields of input, used on the command line to filter, summarize and reformat text and logs.
A cloud-native, statically typed language with built-in support for network services, JSON and concurrency, used to write integrations and API services.
The core SAS programming language, with its data step and procedures, used to read, clean, transform, analyze and report data in the SAS system.
The GNU Bourne-Again shell command language, used to run commands interactively and to write scripts that automate file handling, builds, deployments and administration on Unix-like systems.
A family of beginner-friendly imperative languages dating from 1964, once bundled with microcomputers and now mostly used in teaching and legacy maintenance.
A small Java source interpreter and scripting language that runs Java-like code dynamically, used to embed scripting in Java applications and test tools.
A BASIC-derived, object-oriented compiled language aimed at 2D game and multimedia programming.
A statically typed, Python-inspired language for the .NET and Mono runtimes, once supported as a Unity scripting language.
A low-level, general-purpose procedural language with manual memory management and close hardware access, used for operating systems, embedded firmware, drivers and performance-critical libraries.
Microsoft's object-oriented, statically typed language for the .NET platform, used for web services, desktop applications, games and enterprise software.
A compiled, multi-paradigm extension of C with classes and templates, used for systems software, game engines, trading systems and other performance-critical applications.
ColdFusion Markup Language, the tag-and-script language of Adobe ColdFusion and Lucee used to build dynamic web pages, database-driven applications and web services on the JVM.
A BASIC interpreter for macOS, Linux and Windows that runs classic BASIC programs, used for teaching, hobby programming and legacy code.
Command List, an interpreted scripting language for IBM TSO on z/OS used to automate command sequences and dialogs, largely superseded by REXX.
A modern Lisp for the JVM that emphasizes immutable data, functional programming and concurrency, used for data processing and web back ends.
A verbose, English-like business language that still runs core banking, insurance and government transaction and batch systems on mainframes, maintained and modernized by specialist developers.
A language that compiles to JavaScript with shorter, Ruby- and Python-influenced syntax, found mainly in older web projects.
An early string-processing language developed at MIT in the 1950s for machine translation and linguistics research, now of historical interest.
The ANSI-standardized Lisp dialect with macros, an object system (CLOS) and an interactive REPL workflow, used in AI, symbolic computing and long-lived systems.
An Oberon-descended Pascal-family language for component-based software, associated with the BlackBox Component Builder.
A compiled, statically typed language with Ruby-inspired syntax and type inference, aimed at fast native programs.
A superset of Python that compiles to C extension modules, used to speed up numerical code and to wrap C and C++ libraries.
A compiled systems language with C-like syntax, templates and metaprogramming, used for native applications and tools.
Google's typed, object-oriented language, used with the Flutter framework to build cross-platform mobile, web and desktop apps.
An Object Pascal dialect and development environment from Embarcadero for building native Windows and cross-platform desktop and database applications.
The command and scripting language of OpenVMS, used to run programs, manage files and write job procedures.
A dynamic object-oriented language with Lisp heritage and infix syntax, originally developed at Apple and now a niche language.

The sixth edition of the ECMAScript standard, which added classes, modules, arrow functions, let and const, promises and template literals to JavaScript; working knowledge means writing modern JavaScript.
An object-oriented language built around Design by Contract, with preconditions, postconditions and invariants, used for reliable software and teaching object-oriented design.
A functional, concurrent language on the Erlang virtual machine, used for fault-tolerant web back ends, real-time systems and messaging.
A functional language that compiles to JavaScript for building web front ends, emphasizing reliability and friendly compiler messages.
A functional, concurrent language and runtime designed at Ericsson for fault-tolerant telecommunications systems, used in messaging and distributed back ends.
A functional-first language on .NET with type inference, used for data analysis, domain modeling and back-end services.
A proof-oriented functional language with dependent types and effects, used to verify programs such as cryptographic code.
A statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the JVM, .NET and JavaScript with a portable standard library.
A stack-based, extensible language used in embedded systems and firmware, where programmers define small words and build the language up from them.
One of the oldest high-level languages, still used for array-oriented numerical code in scientific and high-performance computing such as climate, physics and engineering simulation.
A BASIC-style, object-oriented language with a visual development environment for building Linux desktop applications.
A plain-text Given/When/Then language used in Cucumber and similar tools to write behavior-driven development scenarios that run as automated tests.
Google's compiled, statically typed language with goroutines and channels, used for cloud services, command-line tools and infrastructure software.
A query language and runtime for APIs in which clients ask for exactly the fields they need against a typed schema; used to design and consume flexible APIs.
A dynamic JVM language with Java-compatible syntax, used for scripting, Gradle build files and Jenkins pipelines.
Meta's dialect of PHP for the HHVM runtime, adding static typing and asynchronous features.
A purely functional language with lazy evaluation and a strong static type system, used in compilers, finance and research.
A cross-platform language and compiler that targets JavaScript, C++, Java, Python and other runtimes from one code base, used for games and tools.
Microsoft's Java-syntax language for the .NET Framework, now discontinued and met mainly when migrating legacy code.
A statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the Java virtual machine, used for enterprise back ends, Android applications and large systems.
The scripting language of the web, used to make pages interactive in browsers and, through runtimes such as Node.js, to build servers and tooling.
The Java Data Objects Query Language, an object-oriented query language of the JDO API for retrieving persistent Java objects from a datastore.
Microsoft's implementation of ECMAScript, used in Internet Explorer and Windows Script Host and met mostly in legacy scripts.
A JScript variant compiled for the .NET Framework, with optional typing and classes, used in legacy ASP.NET code.
A high-performance dynamic language for numerical and scientific computing with multiple dispatch and just-in-time compilation.
JetBrains' statically typed language for the JVM, Android, JavaScript and native targets, the preferred language for Android development and interoperable with Java.
A graphical PLC programming language, standardized as Ladder Diagram in IEC 61131-3, that expresses control logic as relay-style rungs; used by automation technicians and controls engineers.
The scripting language of Macromedia and Adobe Director, used to program interactive multimedia and games.

flags.note: Not to be confused with LINGO, the optimization modeling language of LINDO Systems.

definition.text: Shopify's open-source template language, used to render dynamic content in Shopify themes, Jekyll sites and email through objects, tags and filters.
A family of languages built on S-expressions with code as data and macros, historically central to AI research and including Common Lisp, Scheme and Clojure.
A CoffeeScript-derived functional language that compiles to JavaScript; also the early name of JavaScript before 1995.

flags.note: Can mean the compile-to-JavaScript language or the original name of JavaScript.

definition.text: An educational language known for turtle graphics, designed to teach children programming and mathematical ideas and descended from Lisp.
A lightweight, embeddable scripting language used for game logic, configuration and application extensions.
MathWorks' matrix-oriented language and environment for numerical computing, data analysis, simulation, signal processing and control design in engineering and science.
MetaQuotes Language 4, the C-like language of the MetaTrader 4 trading platform, used to write automated trading robots and technical indicators.
The Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System, a language with a built-in hierarchical database used in healthcare information systems and some banking systems.
A statically typed compiled language with Python-like syntax and powerful metaprogramming that compiles to C, C++ or JavaScript.
Niklaus Wirth's minimalist successor to Modula-2, also the name of an operating system, used in teaching and language research.
A C superset with Smalltalk-style messaging, the main language of macOS and iOS development before Swift and still found in legacy Apple codebases.
A functional language of the ML family with static typing and type inference, used in compilers, theorem provers and quantitative finance.
Progress Software's Advanced Business Language for building database-centric business applications on the OpenEdge platform, formerly known as Progress 4GL.
A multiparadigm language mixing functional, logic, constraint, object-oriented and concurrent styles, implemented in the Mozart system and used mainly for teaching programming concepts.
Niklaus Wirth's structured, strongly typed teaching language, influential on Delphi, Ada and Modula.
A text-processing and scripting language with strong regular expressions, used for system administration, bioinformatics and legacy web scripts.
A server-side scripting language for web development, behind sites built with WordPress, Laravel and similar systems.
The PHP 7.x release series, which brought large speed gains, scalar type declarations, return types, the null coalescing operator and anonymous classes.
An IBM-designed general-purpose language combining business and scientific features, still found in mainframe systems.
PostgreSQL's procedural language for writing functions, triggers and procedures that run inside the database.
Oracle's procedural extension to SQL for writing stored procedures, functions, packages and triggers that run inside the Oracle database.
Adobe's stack-based page description language that describes printed pages and graphics, used in printing and prepress workflows and as the basis of the early PDF format.
Microsoft's low-code, Excel-like formula language used in Power Apps and other Power Platform tools to build application logic from formulas.
Microsoft's object-oriented shell and scripting language, used by administrators and engineers to automate Windows, Azure and cross-platform systems through cmdlets and pipelines.
A logic programming language in which programs are facts and rules and computation is a query-driven search with backtracking, used in AI, language processing and rule-based systems.
A strongly typed, purely functional language inspired by Haskell that compiles to JavaScript.
A readable, general-purpose language widely used for scripting, web back ends, automation, data analysis and machine learning.
Microsoft's domain-specific language for expressing quantum algorithms, used with the Quantum Development Kit.
A language and environment for statistical computing, data analysis, visualization and reporting, widely used in statistics, bioinformatics and the social sciences.

flags.note: Single-letter name; matching in listings needs exact case and context.

definition.text: A Scheme-descended language for language-oriented programming and teaching, with a macro system for building new languages.
A dynamic, object-oriented language prized for readable syntax, used for web development with Rails, scripting and tooling.
A compiled systems language that guarantees memory safety without garbage collection through ownership and borrowing, used for performance-critical and safe systems software.
The programming language of the SAS analytics system, built from data steps and procedures, used for statistical analysis, reporting and data management in business, healthcare and research.

flags.note: Overlaps Base SAS; the label can also name the SAS software as a whole.

definition.text: The text-substitution and code-generation facility of SAS, used to parameterize and automate SAS programs with macro variables and macros.
A statically typed language combining object-oriented and functional programming on the JVM, used for data engineering with Apache Spark and for back-end services.
A minimalist Lisp dialect with lexical scoping and first-class continuations, used in teaching programming and in language research.
A visual, block-based language from the MIT Media Lab for teaching children programming by snapping blocks together to make games, stories and animations.
Writing scripts for a Unix command shell such as sh, Bash or zsh to chain commands, process files and text, and automate administration, builds and deployments.
A 1960s simulation language that introduced classes and objects, the origin of object-oriented programming.
A pure object-oriented, dynamically typed language and live programming environment in which everything is an object, an influence on Objective-C and Ruby.
The standard language for defining, querying and updating data in relational databases, used for reporting, analysis and application data access.
Apple's compiled, type-safe language for iOS, macOS, watchOS and tvOS applications, also used on servers.
A simple command-based scripting language used for embedding scripts, test automation and tool control, usually paired with the Tk GUI toolkit.
A typed superset of JavaScript from Microsoft that compiles to plain JavaScript, used to build and maintain large web and Node.js applications with static type checking.
Microsoft's query language for Azure Data Lake Analytics, combining SQL-like syntax with C# expressions to process big data; the service has since been retired.
A JavaScript-like language once used for scripting in the Unity game engine, deprecated and removed in favor of C#.
Microsoft's object-oriented successor to classic Visual Basic on the .NET platform, used to build Windows applications and enterprise software.
The Visual Basic dialect embedded in Microsoft Office, in which users write macros and automation to extend Excel, Word, Access and Outlook.
Razor, the markup syntax that mixes C# or Visual Basic code into HTML on ASP.NET pages and views to render dynamic web content.
HyperText Markup Language, the standard markup for structuring web pages; authors use it to define headings, links, forms, media and semantic page structure.
An XML-based format for describing geographic placemarks, paths and overlays for display in Google Earth and other mapping tools.
An XML-based markup used to build user interfaces for Windows Media Center applications.
Adobe Flex's XML-based markup language for declaring the user interface layout and components of Flash and AIR applications.
An OASIS XML standard for exchanging user and resource provisioning requests among identity management systems.
An ISO standard XML-based format and language for describing interactive 3D scenes on the web, successor to VRML.
eXtensible Business Reporting Language, an XML-based standard for tagging financial and business reports so software can exchange and analyze them, used in regulatory filings.
Extensible Markup Language, a W3C text format for structured, self-describing data, used in configuration, data exchange and document formats.
XML User Interface Language, Mozilla's XML markup for describing application interfaces, used by older Firefox and its extensions and now deprecated.
Cascading Style Sheets, the language that describes the visual presentation of web pages, including layout, color, typography and responsive behavior.
A CSS preprocessor language that adds variables, nesting, mixins and functions and compiles to CSS.
A CSS preprocessor with variables, nesting, mixins and modules, written in SCSS or indented syntax and compiled to CSS.
An Open Group modeling language for describing enterprise architecture across business, application and technology layers, used by enterprise architects.
A family of languages for describing the structure and behavior of digital circuits so they can be simulated and synthesized into chips or FPGAs, such as VHDL and Verilog.

flags.note: The label names a language category rather than one language.

definition.text: A Java-based approach to hardware description for designing and simulating FPGA circuits, developed at Brigham Young University.
An IEEE 1800 language that extends Verilog with design and verification features such as classes, assertions and constrained-random testing, used in chip design and verification.
Unified Modeling Language, a standardized visual notation of diagrams such as class, sequence, state and use case for specifying and communicating software design.
A hardware description language for designing and simulating digital circuits at register-transfer level, used in ASIC and FPGA design.
VHSIC Hardware Description Language, a strongly typed language for designing, simulating and synthesizing digital hardware, common in aerospace and FPGA design.

Apple's pressure-sensitive touch technology for iPhone that distinguished light taps from deeper presses to trigger shortcuts and previews; knowledge of it is now needed mainly for legacy iOS interfaces.

flags.note: A discontinued product feature rather than a body of knowledge in the usual sense.

definition.text: The Annular Bearing Engineers' Committee ratings (ABEC 1, 3, 5, 7, 9) that grade the dimensional tolerances of precision ball bearings, used to judge a bearing's precision for an application.

flags.note: A rating standard rather than a field of knowledge.

definition.text: In cellular networks, the identifier naming the gateway a mobile device uses to reach a data network, together with its settings.
In pension accounting, the present value of retirement benefits earned to date, measured on current salaries without projecting future pay increases.
The UN climate convention's term for work on climate education, training, public awareness, public participation and access to information.
The component of a drug product that produces its intended therapeutic effect, with the principles of its manufacture, specification and quality control.
Basic self-care tasks such as bathing, dressing, eating, toileting and moving about, and the assessment of a person's ability to perform them, used in nursing, occupational therapy and eldercare.
The professional examination programs for actuaries, which test probability, financial mathematics, life contingencies, risk and related topics.

flags.note: The label names an exam series, which is closer to a credential; the content knowledge is described here and the canonical class is kept.

definition.text: Knowledge of business and management principles involved in strategic planning, resource allocation, human resources modeling, leadership technique, production methods, and coordination of people and resources.

definition.text: Knowledge of administrative and office procedures and systems such as word processing, managing files and records, stenography and transcription, designing forms, and workplace terminology.
